Cambridge Lower Secondary develops questioning, collaboration, and independent work ahead of the senior school transition. Parel and Lower Parel families, your child's ideal stage is waiting. Schedule your admissions consultation today.

We don't wait for opportunities to come to our students. We help them go after it.

At JBCN International School, Parel, the best IB school in Parel, every student is backed by highly experienced faculty, tailored university counselling, and a strong mentorship culture that makes the journey as rewarding as the destination. Reach out today and take the first step towards a future without limits!

featured_reviews.name: Ahana Sharma
featured_reviews.review_text:
Extremely Disappointing and Unethical Admission Process

We recently relocated from Delhi to Mumbai and inquired about admission at JBCN Parel. Most schools clearly informed us if seats were unavailable at the time of inquiry. However, JBCN’s admission team asked us to purchase an admission kit for ₹5,000 just to apply. Since I have two children, I initially enquired only for my elder one, planning to consider the younger one later. As soon as they found out about my younger child, they insisted that I purchase another ₹5,000 admission kit, claiming it would increase the elder one's chances due to the sibling factor.

They then called us to Mumbai for an interaction. Despite my poor health, I attended the session for my elder child, only to be told that there were no seats and we were placed on a waiting list. Shockingly, they called us back the next day for my younger child’s interaction—only to repeat the same thing: no seats available!

This entire process cost us ₹10,000 for admission kits, flight tickets, and 10 days of hotel expenses—completely wasted on false hopes. They misled us emotionally, mentally, and financially. If there are no seats in a particular branch, the school should not push parents to buy admission kits or schedule interactions.

In contrast, Aditya Birla and Edubridge International School were professional and transparent. They informed us upfront that they didn’t have seats. Edubridge even followed up with us when a seat became available and scheduled a school tour accordingly. This is called professionalism.

To make matters worse, JBCN had the audacity to suggest admission at their Chembur branch, expecting a young child to travel from Lower Parel to Chembur daily—without even providing a bus service!

JBCN, please do better. Admissions should be about a child's education, not just a business model to make money. Stop misleading parents and wasting their time and resources.

featured_reviews.name: Vaishali Pawar
featured_reviews.review_text: This college in Mulund is honestly one of the worst environments for students. There is a complete lack of basic manners, ethics & professionalism among the staff. The way students & even parents are spoken to is extremely disrespectful. Teachers use very casual & inappropriate language that doesn't belong in an educational institution. For example, statements like "aare tu idhar se nikal ja bhai" are used by Regina ma'am which clearly reflects the level of unprofessionalism. Instead of guidance & support, students are often talked down to in a rude & dismissive manner, which is disturbing. The administration focuses more on collecting money than actually supporting students. Fines are imposed for unnecessary reasons, like being late & even mobile phones are confiscated with a ₹500 charge. This feels less like discipline & more like a way to extract money. The management is also highly unprofessional. People are made to wait for hours without proper communication or courtesy. There is no sense of responsibility or respect in how things are handled. Some staff members & teachers like Najuka ma'am blindly follow whatever the principal says, without considering fairness or students well-being. This creates an unhealthy & uncomfortable atmosphere where students feel disturbed rather than motivated. The conduct of the principal is also deeply concerning. The language & tone used at times are inappropriate for someone in a leadership position & it sets a poor example for the entire institution. There appears to be a lack of professionalism, respect & basic etiquette in interactions. A principal is expected to create a positive & respectful environment, but here the leadership style instead contributes to discomfort & dissatisfaction among students. You can basically say that the principal & teachers don't deserve to be here in this position at all. Ironically the only person who showed basic respect & professionalism was the peon of the college. Overall the environment is toxic, disrespectful & not suitable for students who actually want to learn & grow. I would strongly advise students not to take admission here & to choose a better institution. Honestly, this college doesn't even deserve a single star. I've only given one star because it's required to proceed with posting the review on this platform.

owner_posts.post_text: Mulund families no longer need to wonder when the right time is to make the shift to an international school. At JBCN International School Mulund, three entry stages cover every phase of a child's learning journey. The early years, ages 3 to 5, represent the most common and smoothest entry, with play-based inquiry learning nurturing curiosity and language development before academic demands begin. Joining around Grade 6 gives students time to adapt to independent, project-driven learning through the Cambridge Lower Secondary curriculum, without the pressure of senior school exams. From Grade 9 onward, students pursue the IGCSE and then the IB Diploma or A Levels, internationally recognised qualifications sought by universities across the world. The right stage for your child exists at JBCN Mulund. Enquire with our admissions team now.

Aarav Lele has been admitted to Stanford Pre-Collegiate Summer Institutes 2026 for Discrete Mathematics, one of the most competitive pre-college programmes in the world, and he did it while still in school.

We start early, work closely with every student, and make sure no opportunity is missed. This is not luck. This is preparation.

Many parents use "preschool" and "pre-primary" interchangeably, but the two are actually quite distinct.

Preschool is largely play-based, focusing on early socialisation for toddlers aged 2 to 3. Pre-Primary, however, is a structured, curriculum-driven experience for children between 3 and 6 years old, aimed at building school-readiness through language, numeracy, cognitive development, and emotional growth.

At JBCN Mulund, our Pre-Primary programme is designed with far greater purpose than conventional daycare-style learning. With an internationally benchmarked curriculum, skilled educators, and a child-centred approach, we ensure your little one is fully prepared to enter formal schooling with confidence and enthusiasm.

JBCN Pre-Primary Mulund offers:
- Holistic Development
- Internationally Benchmarked Curriculum

- iPropel Skill-Based Programme

CBSE, ICSE, IGCSE, or IB? Choosing the right board shapes your child's entire learning journey. CBSE aligns with Indian competitive exams, ICSE builds depth in language and academics, IGCSE offers global flexibility, and IB develops critical thinking and research skills valued by universities worldwide. The right fit depends on how your child learns, not just rankings or reputation. At JBCN Mulund, learners follow the Cambridge IGCSE and ICSE pathways, combining global academic standards with strong foundational learning. Book a campus visit and find the right fit for your child.

Is your 6-year-old ready for school? At JBCN Mulund, early childhood education is about nurturing strong foundations rather than pushing children to race ahead. Our teachers create engaging, play-based learning experiences that encourage children to explore, question, and grow with joy. As the best international school in Mulund, JBCN provides a warm, structured environment designed to support every child's holistic development.
